== THRESHOLD CONSTANTS AS SHIPPED (PresenceThresholds, InterPresenceEventEngine.swift) ==

PresenceThresholds.parse(json:) consumes rc.activePresenceThresholds — the RAW JSON STRING from /room/join. Empty / malformed / missing keys fall back per key, so a bad field can never silently widen a threshold.

== DETECTOR VERSION STRING ==
The client never invents one. It forwards rc.activePresenceDetectorVersion verbatim ("presence-1.0.0" today) into every payload as `detectorVersion`; the server stamps its own from the session row and discards the client's. An empty string means the key is omitted entirely.

== EXACT PAYLOAD KEYS EMITTED ==
PresenceEvent.asPayload(detectorVersion:) is the ONLY serialisation path in the client (no Codable, no second encoder).
  asPayload()                              -> {eventType, startedAt, endedAt, durationMs}
  asPayload(detectorVersion: "presence-1.0.0") -> + {detectorVersion}
startedAt/endedAt are ISO-8601 UTC STRINGS with fractional seconds (ISO8601DateFormatter, [.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds]) — never numbers, which the server refuses with 400 PRESENCE_PAYLOAD_INVALID. durationMs is a non-negative Int (the init clamps endedAt to >= startedAt so a backwards clock cannot produce a negative). PresenceEvent.allowedPayloadKeys mirrors the server's ALLOWED_EVENT_KEYS and the test asserts the emitted set is a subset.

== THE PRECEDENCE LOCK AS IMPLEMENTED (block comment above the state machine) ==
cameraMuted                        -> emit the camera transition only; close and DISCARD every other open candidate; face_absent cannot open.
detectorFailed || quality < floor  -> feeds image_quality_insufficient ONLY. It MUST NOT feed face_absent.
faceCount == 0 && quality >= floor -> feeds face_absent.
faceCount >= 2                     -> feeds multiple_faces, independently of the quality branch (a frame can be both, and the honest record is both).
THE CRITICAL RULE is a named comment in the engine AND in the detector: a detection failure is a data-quality fact about the VIDEO (image_quality_insufficient) and NEVER face_absent, which would attribute it to the candidate's behaviour (§7.1, §4.1). Three passing tests assert events.contains { $0.eventType == "face_absent" } is false for detector failure, for confidence below the floor and for box area below the floor.

== THE ONE DESIGN DECISION FEAT-004 MUST DOCUMENT: THE EMPTY-RESULT SENTINEL ==
§7.1's quality rule is literal in the engine (detectorFailed OR minConfidence < 0.35 OR maxBoxAreaFraction < 0.01), which means the DETECTOR has to say what those two numbers mean for a result with no faces. A successful VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest that found nobody returns the NEUTRAL sentinels maxBoxAreaFraction 1.0 / minConfidence 1.0 — "the request ran, there is no quality objection against this frame" — so a genuine absence is recorded as face_absent. Zeroes there would have made every real absence an image_quality_insufficient and face_absent unreachable. A thrown error or nil results sets detectorFailed = true instead. Both branches are asserted (testAdapterEmptyResultIsNotAQualityObjection, testEmptySuccessfulDetection_yieldsFaceAbsent_notImageQuality, testAdapterFailedSampleIsAQualityObjection).

== CAMERA DISCIPLINE, ALL SEVEN INVARIANTS ==
Enforced in InterPresenceCaptureSource (header comment lists them numbered) and asserted in InterPresenceCaptureSourceTests:
1 exactly one AVCaptureVideoDataOutput of its own, added and removed inside beginConfiguration/commitConfiguration guarded by canAddOutput (outputsAdded == outputsRemoved; a foreign output added before start is still present after stop);
2 videoSettings pinned to kCVPixelFormatType_32BGRA, alwaysDiscardsLateVideoFrames true;
3 NEVER startRunning/stopRunning (AVCaptureSession subclass flags the calls: 0; sessionRunCalls 0; session.isRunning false throughout);
4 NEVER addInput/removeInput (same subclass flags: 0; inputs identical by count AND identity before start / after stop);
5 never touches a LiveKit track and never calls mute()/unmute() — the class imports no LiveKit at all;
6 returns immediately while the camera state is .muted or .muting (framesSampled 0, framesSkippedMuted 10, zero pixel buffers reach the detector);
7 does NOT co-opt InterLocalMediaController.recordingFrameObserver or recordingCameraStateObserver — neither symbol appears in any new file.
Delegate queue is "inter.presence.detect" at .utility (below the publisher's .userInteractive). 2 Hz throttle uses the frame's own presentation timestamp: 30 frames 100 ms apart yield exactly 6 sampled and 24 throttled.

== HOW THE CAMERA STATE REACHES THE ENGINE (not spelled out in the plan — read this before changing it) ==
The frame path cannot observe a camera switch-off, because the frames simply stop. The coordinator therefore runs its own 500 ms DispatchSourceTimer on "inter.presence.camera" (.utility) that reads cameraEnabledProvider() — a block the ONE call site builds over InterLocalMediaController.isCameraEnabled (an `atomic` ObjC property, so the read is thread-safe, and the block captures the controller strongly so it cannot dangle). On a transition it pushes setCameraState() into the capture source, and while the camera is off it feeds the engine PresenceSample.cameraOff, which is what emits camera_disabled (durationMs 0) and discards the other open candidates. camera_enabled lands on the first real frame back. NO new observer slot was taken and NO extra call site was added: the provider block is created inside the single guarded `if`.

== INDICATOR STATE, SINGLE WRITER ==
The coordinator is the single writer while monitoring runs, using FEAT-002's 0/1/2/3 encoding through -setPresenceMonitoringState:. It pushes 1 at a successful start, 3 for as long as the camera is off, 1 again when it returns, and 2 on stop(), on an ingest 403/409 (via the reporter's monitoringOffHandler) and when the session refuses the detector output or the room context is incomplete. Pushes are deduplicated and always hopped to the main queue (the chrome bridge is @MainActor).
ONE HONEST CAVEAT, by design and not fixable inside this FEAT: AppDelegate's -startCandidatePresenceSurface (FEAT-002) still writes the chip from the consent decision and from the server's consent response. It has to, because on a DECLINE the coordinator never starts and the chip must still read "off". Ordering makes a conflict practically impossible — the consent POST completes within milliseconds of enterMode, while the coordinator only starts after the camera-permission/prepare round trip — and a human camera toggle is seconds later. FEAT-004 should record this as "the coordinator owns 1 and 3; AppDelegate owns the initial and declined 2".

== REPORTER BEHAVIOUR ON THE WIRE ==
15.0 s DispatchSourceTimer plus a flush on stop, through InterTokenService.uploadPresenceEvents(serverURL:roomCode:identity:events:completion:) — the FEAT-002 method. An EMPTY batch IS POSTED, because that is the heartbeat the server's monitoring_gap detection depends on. Buffer cap 200, overflow drops the OLDEST and counts eventsDropped. A transient network error re-inserts the batch at the FRONT (order preserved) subject to the same cap. HTTP 403 or 409 stops reporting for good, clears the buffer and reports monitoring-off upward. Not one byte of pixel data can reach it: PresenceEvent has no member able to hold a buffer, image, Data or series, and asPayload() is the only encoder.

== DEVIATIONS FROM THE PLAN, WITH REASONS ==
1. start() does NOT take `thresholds:`; the coordinator takes `thresholdsJSON:` on its INITIALISER instead (plan item 19c lists thresholds as a start parameter). The capture source's 2 Hz interval comes out of the same snapshot, so it has to be known before the source is built. Same data, same source, one parse.
2. start() gained `tokenService:` and `serverURL:`, which the plan's signature omitted. The reporter needs an uploader and plan item 19b names InterTokenService.uploadPresenceEvents as the one upload path; the alternative (handing the coordinator the whole InterRoomController) would have coupled the detector to room state it has no business reading.
3. The coordinator owns a 500 ms camera watchdog that the plan does not mention. Without it a camera switch-off is invisible to the detector (frames just stop), so an open face_absent would hang unevaluated and the paused indicator would never appear. See "HOW THE CAMERA STATE REACHES THE ENGINE" above. It adds no call site and takes no observer slot.
4. InterPresenceDetectorTests drives the Vision adapter through `PresenceFaceReading` values rather than synthetic VNFaceObservations (plan item 20 asks for the latter). VNFaceObservation.confidence is read-only and cannot be synthesised, and the only public factory for one takes the roll/yaw arguments this feature must not touch at all. InterPresenceDetector.sample(from:) is the SHIPPING function analyse(pixelBuffer:) calls with exactly those numbers, and one test additionally runs a real VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest end to end over a blank BGRA frame (asserts no face found, counter incremented, no crash).
5. InterPresenceCaptureSourceTests proves "never touches session inputs" with an AVCaptureSession subclass that FLAGS addInput/removeInput/startRunning/stopRunning rather than with the pre-added dummy input plan item 21 describes. An AVCaptureDeviceInput cannot be constructed without opening a real camera or microphone, which in a test runner means a TCC prompt and a hung suite. The flagging subclass is the stronger assertion anyway: a source that never calls removeInput cannot remove anybody's input, pre-added or not.
6. The pinned-format assertion reads InterPresenceCaptureSource.pinnedVideoSettings (the dictionary makeDetectorOutput() applies) plus AVFoundation's own availableVideoPixelFormatTypes, not the output's videoSettings getter. Measured on this machine: an AVCaptureVideoDataOutput reports videoSettings back as nil when fresh, after assignment, and after being added to a session with no camera input — so a camera-free unit test cannot read the pin back. Recorded in a comment on the test.
7. The §7.1 quality rule is implemented literally, which forced the empty-result sentinel decision documented above. It is the only place the engine's behaviour depends on a convention the detector chose rather than on a number the plan gave.
8. The engine's injected time is Unix epoch seconds (Date().timeIntervalSince1970), not a monotonic clock, because the server demands ISO-8601 stamps and a monotonic value cannot be converted to a date. A backwards clock step can therefore shorten a duration but can never make it negative (the PresenceEvent init clamps).
